papers.citation: Bhosale et al. (2025). Assessing LEO Satellite Networks for National Emergency Failover. DOI: 10.1145/3730567.3764482
papers.reading_notes: Full twenty-page paper, Algorithms 1–2, evaluation, bibliography, appendices and figures reviewed. Findings are optimistic simulation bounds conditioned on coordinated deployment, working gateways and no competing traffic. No physical nationwide failover was measured. Table 1 prints Lithuania capacity 2,005 Gbps, lost cable capacity 101 Gbps and 198 percent; the two capacities instead imply 1,985.15 percent. We preserve the published capacity values and flag the inconsistent percentage without inferring which printed field is wrong.

papers.citation: Suvam Basak, Amitangshu Pal, and Debopam Bhattacherjee. 2025.{LEOCraft}: Towards Designing Performant{LEO} Networks. In 2025 USENIX Annual Technical Conference (USENIX ATC 25) . 789–813.
papers.reading_notes: Full twenty-six-page proceedings PDF, including cover, appendices, code listings and artifact instructions, reviewed. LEOCraft uses process-parallel orbital geometry and flow models to optimize trajectories/topologies. Throughput is a multi-commodity linear program restricted to twenty shortest candidate paths, with gravity-model demand, equal feeder bandwidth sharing, free-space/Shannon rates and fifty-Gbps four-ISL connectivity. These differ from CosmoSim national downlink maximum flow and its three-ISL graph. Domain-informed variable-neighborhood search accelerates tested designs but establishes heuristic improvements rather than global optimality; optimization comparisons use empirically chosen iteration budgets. Hypatia agreement validates selected propagation RTTs, not total capacity. Inter-shell handovers, obstruction and interference remain qualified limitations. Code and artifact instructions aid reproducibility, while traffic/gateway and PHY assumptions prevent direct empirical emergency-service claims.

Vaibhav Bhosale, Ketan Bhardwaj, and Ahmed Saeed. 2023. Astrolabe: modeling RTT variability in Leo networks. In Proceedings of the 1st ACM Workshop on LEO Networking and Communication. 7–12.
papers.reading_notes: Full six-page text reviewed. Astrolabe estimates propagation RTT bounds for shortest-path ISL networks using orbital geometry; validation uses Hypatia simulations of city pairs rather than physical national capacity measurements. Lower bounds use chords to avoid arc overestimation, and upper bounds deliberately overestimate routes across planes. The model is conditional on routing/topology and omits operational delay sources. Supports orbital-state sensitivity and the need to distinguish geometric bounds from measured service performance.

papers.citation: Vaibhav Bhosale, Ahmed Saeed, Ketan Bhardwaj, and Ada Gavrilovska. 2023. A characterization of route variability in leo satellite networks. In International Conference on Passive and Active Network Measurement . Springer, 313–342.
papers.reading_notes: Full twenty-nine-page author paper and references reviewed. Hypatia geometry at one-second updates characterizes shortest-path lifetimes, usage and RTTs over complete 100–110-minute orbits; Mahimahi/Pantheon separately emulate selected delay/bandwidth traces. Greedy routing can abandon usable paths for small RTT gains and concentrate many city pairs onto one path. Congestion-control results use one selected sixty-second route and deliberately alternating bandwidth levels, so they illustrate sensitivity rather than measure national deployment performance. ISL geometry is relatively stable; variable GSL availability and route composition create spatially structured RTT changes. Four-ISL phased grids, independent shells and no ground relays differ from our model. Additional satellite shells help variability only for certain inclinations/altitudes. Supports future service-continuity and application tests beyond static capacity snapshots.

papers.version_note: Retrieved sixteen-page IAC-18-B2.1.7 conference text describing September 2018 filings; the citation names the 2019 Acta Astronautica journal article. This precursor is not asserted identical to the cited final version.
papers.reading_notes: Full available text reviewed. Historical SpaceX/OneWeb/Telesat comparison combines demand, ITU atmospheric attenuation, DVB-S2X link budgets, genetic ground-site selection and minimum-cost maximum flow. Daily 60-second orbital states and independent weather draws model capacity distributions; ISL analysis subsamples feeder-capacity quantiles. Demand assumes 10% market capture and 300 kbps per user, with no obstruction, power shortfall, competing-constellation interference or landing-right restrictions. Ground sites and gateway antennas have different roles and counts. Shows why rate, demand and gateway assumptions materially affect bounds, but historical global sellable capacity is not empirical national emergency capacity.

papers.citation: Birkan Denizer, Nils Dohse, and Olaf Landsiedel. 2025. FjordLink: Comparison of Starlink and 5G Networks for Teleoperated Vessel Control. InProceedings of the 2025 3rd Workshop on LEO Networking and Communication . 8–14.
papers.reading_notes: Full seven-page article and repository cover reviewed. Four-month Kiel-Fjord vessel campaign combines Starlink FHP and two 5G networks using TWAMP and fixed-target UDP throughput. The 50-Mbps downlink target censors achievable capacity; an uplink shortfall is distinct from national downlink failover. Measurement rates, moving/docked sample counts and terrestrial PoP delays differ. Trace emulation shows BBR throughput/retransmission tradeoffs, not a change to satellite aggregate capacity. Priority traffic, local cellular coverage, mounting and geographic selection limit generalization.

papers.citation: John S Downs, Bruce Barbour, Alexander Kedrowitsch, Deven Mhadgut, Suryansh Aryan, and Samantha P Kenyon. 2025. Space Network (SpaceNet) TestbedDevelopment of a Multi-Functional Testbed for Simulating Space Communication Networks. In AIAA SCITECH 2025 Forum . 2716.
papers.version_note: Eighteen-page Virginia Tech accepted manuscript of the cited AIAA SCITECH 2025 article; final typeset equivalence is not asserted.
papers.reading_notes: Full eighteen-page text and references reviewed. SpaceNet precomputes Skyfield states, four-neighbor PlusGrid links and shortest-latency routes, then runs Mininet on the paths relevant to selected ground-station pairs. Twelve scenarios compare ideal and actual 1,584-satellite shells at two epochs, with twelve ten-second states and one trial each. Network transitions are paused out of ping measurements. Actual TLE irregularity can create more than four bidirectional ISLs per satellite; latency outliers may reflect emulator artifacts rather than orbital effects. SDR/Raspberry Pi hardware integration demonstrates connectivity at about two Mbps, not national capacity. Weather-dependent ground links and hardware integration are capabilities, while higher-fidelity ground links and resiliency remain future work. Supports reporting emulation overhead, routing assumptions and transition exclusions separately; path pruning cannot preserve national maximum flow without additional validation.

In Proceedings of the 2015 ACM Conference on Special Interest Group on Data Communication (London, United Kingdom) (SIGCOMM ’15). Association for Computing Machinery, New York, NY, USA, 565–578. https://doi.org/10.1145/2785956.2787499
papers.reading_notes: Full fourteen-page paper reviewed. Constructs an incomplete US long-haul conduit map from operator maps, rights-of-way and public records, then overlays traceroutes to examine shared infrastructure. Logical provider diversity can conceal common physical conduits. Risk rankings use sharing and route-frequency proxies, not failure probabilities or observed byte-volume loss; hidden MPLS paths and geolocation errors remain limits. Suggested backup paths/new conduits improve modeled sharing metrics, but physical rights-of-way and deployment costs constrain feasibility. Historical legal discussion is not current policy guidance. Supports explicit shared-failure dependencies and separate cable capacity versus traffic-loss measures; it does not independently validate satellite failover.

papers.reading_notes: Full twenty-six-page HitchHiking paper, references and all appendices reviewed. TTL-specific ICMP probes subtract the last visible pre-satellite hop from the customer hop, then smooth at fifteen seconds. Ground truth from one San Diego dish supports latency accuracy, while 2,473 exposed endpoints broaden geographic coverage but represent about 0.1% of users and exclude jittery paths. Measurements include gateway-to-PoP fiber and cannot directly identify satellite/ISL paths. Sustained-delay explanations combine physical lower bounds, customer location and operator confirmation; individual path assignments remain inferences. OneWeb extension lacks equipment-based validation. Important counterevidence to interpreting shortest-path physics as deployed network behavior: PoP anchoring and remote-gateway routing can increase latency. Does not measure national aggregate failover bandwidth or prove that observed endpoint samples represent all subscribers.

papers.reading_notes: Full preprint text reviewed. Mininet-based platform precomputes orbital/link/routing states, applies only changing links and prunes to paths relevant to selected flows. Scalability comparisons depend on implementation, machine and flow selection; preparation cost is separate from real-time updates. papers.citation: Kassing, Simon and Bhattacherjee, Debopam and Águas, André Baptista and Saethre, Jens Eirik and Singla, Ankit. 2020. Exploring the “Internet from space” with Hypatia. In Proc. of ACM IMC ’20 . 214–229.
papers.reading_notes: Full sixteen-page Hypatia paper, bibliography and bent-pipe appendix reviewed. Separates precomputed TLE/connectivity/forwarding states from ns-3 packet events and Cesium visualization. Its default four-ISL topology and FCC-era constellations differ from CosmoSim's three-ISL design. Static snapshots match most propagation RTTs but miss packets taking detours during route changes; one-second updates miss changes that 100-ms updates preserve. Loss-free handoffs and absent RF interference are favorable assumptions. TCP can misinterpret reordering as loss or orbital RTT increases as congestion, and changing cross-traffic leaves bandwidth unused. These results motivate temporal and application validation; they do not validate aggregate national maximum flow as achievable service.

papers.version_note: Thirteen-page author manuscript; references include 2025 material whereas the main bibliography gives a September 2023 preprint date. Exact-version equivalence is not asserted.
papers.reading_notes: Full text and equations reviewed. Models Starlink/Kuiper shared-band downlinks with phased-array gains, power-flux limits, 0.1-second states and ten clusters of 127 cells. Lagrangian/subgradient satellite selection trades time-averaged protection, absolute interference peaks and secondary utilization; dual bounds do not automatically prove global optimality of an integer solution. Interference protection is a proposed operating constraint, not evidence of regulatory acceptance. Intra-system interference is omitted. Learned primary associations have modest top-one accuracy, while more conservative candidate sets reduce utilization. Establishes that cross-constellation interference and handover-window choices can change usable capacity, both absent from our idealized fixed-rate national model.

StarryNet: Empowering Researchers to Evaluate Futuristic Integrated Space and Terrestrial Networks. In USENIX Symposium on Networked Systems Design and Implementation (NSDI) . USENIX.
papers.reading_notes: Full seventeen-page proceedings file, including cover and references, reviewed. StarryNet combines observed orbital/configuration data, Skyfield states and distributed Docker/Open vSwitch emulation; VLANs preserve topology and precomputed updates reduce orchestration overhead. Capacity is user-configured and validation tunes rates to an existing terminal trace, so matching that trace is calibration rather than independent aggregate-capacity validation. OSPF experiments expose reconvergence and address-change disruptions; hardware-in-loop demonstrates processor/power effects on one prototype. Public TLE accuracy, missing ISL details and limited PHY fidelity constrain the digital twin. Supports distinguishing network service/recovery behavior from static maximum-flow bounds.

papers.citation: Dominic Laniewski, Eric Lanter, Simon Beainn, Jan Dunker, Michael Dückers, and Nils Aschenbruck. 2024. Starlink on the Road: A First Look at Mobile Starlink Performance in Central Europe. In 2024 8th Network Traffic Measurement and Analysis Conference (TMA). IEEE, 1–8.
papers.reading_notes: Full eight-page text reviewed. Two-month German service-van campaign logs 15,269 samples, including 4,196 while moving, with FHP dish, UDP tests, ping, route and power data. Throughput drops with motion but correlations with actual speed are weak; high-speed groups are sparse and route obstructions confound attribution. Priority and hardware differ from stationary comparison data. Power samples are much fewer than network samples; startup and winter heating confound motion-power effects. Battery charging limits prevented fully autonomous operation. Emphasizes deployability and power constraints excluded from idealized national capacity.

papers.reading_notes: Models one rural forested vehicle route with 100 randomized orbital starting times, SGP4 geometry, Blender/OSM terrain and canopy-height meshes. The authors identify simplified attenuation, additional routes and physical drive-test validation as future work. Supports obstruction and scheduler sensitivity as untested limitations of our fixed-rate national maximum-flow model. papers.reading_notes: Full seven-page author text reviewed. Compares January-2021 filed Telesat, OneWeb, Starlink and Kuiper designs using population demand, ITU atmospheric attenuation, link budgets, optimized ground segments and maximum flow. Evaluates 1,440 daily orbital scenarios with 10,000 atmospheric samples per scenario. Initial and final phases use different elevation-angle assumptions; some ISL configurations are hypothetical. papers.citation: Nils Pachler de la Osa. 2024. Optimizing resource allocation in large communications satellite constellations . Ph. D. Dissertation. Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
papers.reading_notes: Full 315-page MIT doctoral dissertation, including four appendices and bibliography, reviewed. Decomposes beam/user grouping, satellite/frequency allocation and gateway routing into sequential heuristic or mixed-integer subproblems; subproblem optimization is not global optimality. Link-budget checks compare earlier models, not field ground truth. Annual weather statistics, fixed population demand and same-system interference add realism, but sufficient satellite power, instantaneous handovers, unobstructed terminals and no competing constellations remain favorable assumptions. The historical SpaceX link example yields 0.956 Gbps at zenith and 0.823 Gbps at forty degrees. Gateway antennas differ from station sites; routing candidates and hop limits restrict the feasible set. Capacity, design rankings and LEO/MEO benefits change with demand and interference assumptions. The surrogate permits simultaneous multi-satellite terminal service and omits some operational restrictions. Failure robustness and real-time adaptation are future work. Supports conditional capacity bounds and separate continuity experiments, not empirical national emergency validation.

papers.citation: Nils Pachler de la Osa, Markus Guerster, Inigo del Portillo Barrios, Edward Crawley, and Bruce Cameron. 2021. Static beam placement and frequency plan algorithms for LEO constellations. International Journal of Satellite Communications and Networking 39, 1 (2021), 65–77.
papers.version_note: Thirteen-page author typeset text carries 2020 acceptance and citation information; main bibliography dates the journal volume 2021.
papers.reading_notes: Full paper and algorithms reviewed. Static beam placement groups fixed users using worst-case angular separation and randomized clique heuristics; first-fit frequency planning enforces interference and satellite-group reuse constraints. Evaluation uses historical 4,409-satellite geometry and 18,712 proprietary projected terminals. Small cases permit optimality checks; larger cases only establish improvement over selected baselines, with about 2.3% of beams unassigned. Pairwise angular compatibility is a modeling approximation to physical beam coverage. Caption and body give inconsistent India example counts. Static plans, conservative satellite grouping and omitted joint power optimization differ from CosmoSim's state-specific greedy allocation; radio-coverage heuristics are not proven national service optima.

papers.reading_notes: Full fourteen-page paper reviewed. Network Syntax relates traceroute-derived AS-link popularity to traffic ground truth from one Tier-1 ISP and one IXP across 2011/2013 datasets. Strong correlations primarily apply to transformed, clustered links, not calibrated individual cable-byte volumes.
